summary: Abraham again identifies Sarah as his sister, and Abimelech king of Gerar takes her. God warns Abimelech in a dream, acknowledges his ignorance and restraint, and orders Sarah restored; Abimelech challenges Abraham, returns Sarah with gifts, and Abraham prays for the household’s fertility to return.
whyItMatters: The repetition of Abraham’s protective deception places Sarah in another ruler’s power, while the ruler’s own protest challenges Abraham’s conduct. The chapter refuses a simple division between a righteous ancestor and a guilty foreign king.

context.author: Genesis names no historical writer. Jewish and Christian tradition associates the Torah with Moses; the book briefing describes older traditions shaped into a final literary form, without a settled account of every stage.
context.audience: The book addresses Israel through a story of shared human origins and the family from whom Israel traces its ancestry; no single first audience is named in this chapter.
context.date: The narrated events belong to primeval or ancestral time, not to a securely dated writing event. Major stages of Genesis are often placed across the monarchic to Persian periods, with exact models and dates debated.
context.setting: Gerar and Abimelech’s household during Abraham and Sarah’s residence as foreigners.
context.literaryForm: Wife-sister deception and dream-warning narrative followed by confrontation, restoration, and healing.

before.text: After Sodom’s destruction and Lot’s cave episode, Abraham moves toward the South and lives in Gerar. He again calls Sarah his sister.

here.text: Listen to Abimelech’s defense, God’s acknowledgment of his integrity, and his direct challenge to Abraham before Sarah is restored.

after.text: Sarah bears Isaac as promised, and a celebration of the child leads to a new conflict involving Hagar and Ishmael.

outline.heading: Sarah taken and dream warning
outline.note: Abraham’s sister claim leads Abimelech to take Sarah and receive a warning.

outline.heading: Abimelech’s innocence and restoration command
outline.note: God acknowledges that he had not touched Sarah and orders her return.

outline.heading: Ruler confronts Abraham
outline.note: Abimelech challenges the deception; Abraham explains fear and his half-sibling claim.

outline.heading: Sarah restored; household healed
outline.note: Gifts accompany Sarah’s return, and Abraham prays after the household’s wombs were closed.

keyVerses.text: Didn’t he tell me, ‘She is my sister’? She, even she herself, said, ‘He is my brother.’ I have done this in the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my hands.”
keyVerses.why: Abimelech explicitly protests that both spouses supplied the misleading sibling claim.

keyVerses.text: God said to him in the dream, “Yes, I know that in the integrity of your heart you have done this, and I also withheld you from sinning against me. Therefore I didn’t allow you to touch her.
keyVerses.why: God acknowledges Abimelech’s integrity and says he was kept from touching Sarah.

keyVerses.text: Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said to him, “What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? You have done deeds to me that ought not to be done!”
keyVerses.why: The foreign king’s moral challenge to Abraham is central to the scene.

questions.question: Why does Abraham call Sarah his sister again?
questions.answer: He says he feared people in Gerar would kill him to take her and had asked her to use this claim wherever they traveled. He also says she is his father’s daughter but not his mother’s, which explains a partial truth without undoing the deception about their marriage.

questions.question: Does Sarah choose to enter Abimelech’s household?
questions.answer: The chapter says Abimelech sends for and takes her after the sister claim; it does not record her consent to that removal. God later says Abimelech did not touch her, but the lack of sexual contact does not erase her being taken.

questions.question: What does “integrity” mean in Abimelech’s defense?
questions.answer: He says he acted without knowing Sarah was married because both Abraham and Sarah called each other siblings. God agrees that his heart was sincere and says he prevented further wrongdoing.

questions.question: Why is Abimelech threatened when he did not know?
questions.answer: God warns of death because Sarah is married, then acknowledges Abimelech’s innocence and tells him to restore her. The passage keeps the warning and the recognition together rather than portraying him as a knowing seducer.

questions.question: How does Abimelech respond when he learns the truth?
questions.answer: He tells his servants, confronts Abraham over the danger brought on his kingdom, asks for an explanation, and then restores Sarah with gifts. His speech says Abraham acted in a way that ought not be done.

questions.question: What role does Abraham’s prayer have?
questions.answer: God directs Abimelech to return Sarah and says Abraham will pray for him. After the restoration, Abraham does pray and God heals Abimelech’s household; the narrative connects prayer with recovery rather than with permission for deception.

questions.question: Why are women in Abimelech’s household affected?
questions.answer: The closing verse says their wombs were closed because of Sarah, and the prior verse says healing restored births. The text does not explain their individual fault, so their suffering should not be treated as proof they knowingly participated.

questions.question: What does living as a “foreigner” mean for Abraham here?
questions.answer: He resides in Gerar outside his ancestral home and explains his fear as a stranger in an unknown place. That setting helps explain his thinking but does not settle whether his strategy was fair to Sarah or Abimelech.

glossary.def: The place where Abraham lives temporarily and where King Abimelech takes Sarah.
Sincerity or honest intention, claimed by Abimelech and acknowledged by God in the dream.
The title God gives Abraham when directing Abimelech to restore Sarah and receive his prayer.
